branch_purpose: Theoretical continuation on protocol-preserving catalyst removal and sequential channel cost, kept independent of the existing theoretical-pro checkpoint head.

assumptions: Finite-dimensional bipartite channel and fixed product replacement channel.
Early task announces the common flag before the fresh input, which may be selected in response; late task receives the input before producing the flag.
Adaptive external distinguishing error is normalized to [0,1].

Exact catalysts are returned as marginals at the end of the complete simulation for every allowed input interaction; correlations with retained outputs are allowed and catalyst dimensions are arbitrary finite values.

costs.limitations: Direct routing identities are source claims. Strict positivity for the example uses the N683 sequential-cost classification. No unrestricted memoryless parallel cost theorem or efficient algorithm is established.
costs.reported_identity: E_early^cat(H_{p,N}) = p E_seq^cat(N), with the analogous unassisted identity, as claimed in the source.
